Thanks for the ping — I pulled the attached payload and logs. Initial read and repro guidance below.

Initial hypothesis
1) Payload size / token limit: Their average doc length (~400 tokens) * batch 16 => worst-case token processing could exceed the model max sequence length in some batches, which can trigger runtime failures in the backend (we sometimes see that as 5xx from the runtime).
2) Upstream proxy timeouts: client timeout=10s looks low for large batch scoring; if requests hit queueing and kernel selection, it's plausible they hit a 504 at the proxy layer.
3) Malformed JSON or trailing commas in payload can trigger parser-level 500s — logs don't strongly indicate this, but worth checking the exact Content-Type and SDK serialization.

Immediate repro steps for customer (send these to Sam):
- Increase client timeout to 30s (or disable early client-side timeout) while we triage.
- Reduce batch_size to 4 and re-run a few batches; if errors disappear, it's batch-size related.
- Set stream=false in the request body (they may be using streaming with small timeouts).
- Confirm request header: Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and no extra commas.

Debugging on our side
- Ask Sam for one of the raw X-Redwood-Request-Id values from the logs (I'll look up the full trace and kernel logs).
- I'll try to repro locally using their request_payload_20260514.json and our reranker-v1-large model with the same SDK version. I'll also share a curl reproduction command: 

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @request_payload_20260514.json \
  --max-time 60 \

Notes / quick mitigations
- If this is runtime token limit: we can suggest truncation or switching to a reranker-v1-fast for larger batches.
- If this is proxy timeout: we can ask infra to bump the proxy 60s threshold for this customer's requests temporarily while we root cause.

I'll start local repro now and update the thread with request ids. If infra needs to be paged, message me and I'll escalate.

—Nikhil

Adding a few infra/optimizer tips from my side:

1) KV-cache / prefix caching: If they're reusing the same context across batches, enabling prefix caching dramatically reduces token processing time. Ask if they can pin common context.
2) Quantization/profile: For reranker-v1-large, suggest the "q4_0-high" profile if they want latency over absolute output fidelity; this can reduce processing time per request.
3) Embedding-reranker alignment: ensure the embeddings they send match the dimension / normalization expected by the reranker model. Mismatched dims can sometimes cause internal errors.

Customer-facing suggestions to try first:
- Reduce batch_size -> 4 and set client timeout to 30s.
- Switch to reranker-v1-fast for a short test (we can point them to the model alias).
- Enable SDK debug tracing (redwood-js: set REDWOOD_DEBUG=transport) and share the trace file.

I'll help repro locally and can offer to join a call tomorrow morning to walk through the trace.

—Neha
